subject: Embeddings validation — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Embeddings validation — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Sara —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

1) Current ask / goals
- Improve semantic search recall for product catalog (short descriptions) and reduce false positives in top-10 results.
- Monitor drift over next quarter and set alerts for quality regressions.

2) What we ran in the call
- Live k-NN demo with your sample of 5k product descriptions
- Baseline: your current model (vendor-provided) vs. Redwood-hosted embeddings runs

3) Initial recommendations
- Model: try RW-Embed-Large-v2 (768d, float16) for best recall; fallback RW-Embed-Base-v1 (384d) if you need lower cost/latency.
- Dimensionality note: 768d gave ~3–4% mAP lift in our quick run, but we should measure disk/latency tradeoffs for your scale.
- Normalization: use cosine on L2-normalized vectors; shard index by product category for faster warm queries.

4) Next steps / action items
- I will share the benchmark outputs (CSV) + the prompt set used for similarity checks by EOD today. (See attachments.)
- Sara: please send a sample of your full-text product descriptions (up to 50k rows) or provide S3/Drive access so we can run a 50k job.
- Marissa/Rishi: schedule a 90-minute deep-dive next week to run a full validation with your evaluation metrics and drift checks.

Links & artifacts:
- Embeddings benchmark folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-embeddings-benchmarks
- HubSpot record: HS-12345

Attachments: embeddings_benchmarks_q1_2027.csv, prompt_sets_v2.md

Thanks — looking forward to the 50k run.
— Marcus

Thanks Marcus — super helpful recap. A couple quick questions before we share the larger dataset:

- For the RW-Embed-Large-v2 recommendation: what are the expected qps/latency numbers on a single dedicated GPU (NVIDIA A10G) for 768d when running ANN search?
- How sensitive is the mAP improvement to prompt set changes? If we slightly alter the tokenization/normalization of descriptions, should we expect big swings?

We'll provision an S3 bucket with 50k sample rows by tomorrow and share access. Also, can you flag any potential privacy concerns when we upload product descriptions (some fields may contain PII from merchant notes)?

— Sara

sara.jones@acme.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings validation — post-call recap and next steps

Sara — great questions. Quick answers below and some detail to help you plan the S3 upload.

- Latency / QPS on A10G (approximate):
  - RW-Embed-Large-v2 (768d, float16): embedding latency ~9–12 ms per request with batching (batch=64); ANN (FAISS HNSW/pq) top-10 query latency ~6–12 ms depending on index config. Rough QPS: 500–1,200/sec sustained on a well-provisioned single A10G for mixed embed + search workloads.
  - RW-Embed-Base-v1 (384d): ~5–7 ms embed latency; ANN search ~4–8 ms. QPS scales roughly 1.5–2x vs 768d.

- Sensitivity to prompt set / normalization:
  - We saw modest sensitivity: small tokenization/stopword differences caused 1–3% mAP variance in our internal tests, while larger rewrites (changing granularity of descriptions) produced bigger shifts.
  - We'll include the prompt_sets_v2.md we used and recommend locking a canonical normalization (lowercase, simple punctuation strip, preserve numeric specs) as part of your pipeline before running the canonical evaluation.

- PII & privacy: product descriptions sometimes include merchant notes — recommend removing or hashing any obvious PII fields before we ingest. If you prefer, you can give us a read-only S3 prefix and we can run the job in your account (Redwood Private / Dedicated options) so the data never leaves your environment.

I'll have Marissa set up the deep-dive once you confirm S3 access.

— Marcus
